question: In the context of the review of the IEA for the Taranto steel plant, Italian legislation provides for the addition of a programme agreement, Articles 10 and 11 of which defer health data and commitments to stages following the release of the authorisation.

Under Requirement No 2, the final investigation opinion requires the operator to submit an update to the health impact study within three months of the release of the IEA, including NO₂ and SO₂, emissions data from the power plant and exposure scenarios in public and coastal areas.

The Istituto Superiore di Sanità (National Health Institute – ISS) is able to express its views only 30 days after the document has been sent. Further problems reported by the ISS1 were postponed with deadlines of between 3 and 24 months.
In the light of Directive 2010/75/EU and the judgment of the Court of Justice in Case C626/22, which require a comprehensive and preventive assessment of health and environmental risks: 1.
Is it compatible with that directive to issue the IEA before the mandatory health assessments?
Does the Commission consider it fair to make the ISS’s opinion subject to postauthorisation requirements?
Will it verify compliance with the directive and the legitimacy of making the review subject to a programme agreement?
Requirements Nos 73, 74, 76, 77, 78 and 80 a/b.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.11.

2025) In its judgment of 25 June 2024 in Case C-626/221, the Court of Justice of the EU ruled that the Industrial Emissions Directive (IED)2 must be interpreted as meaning that the Member States are required to provide that the prior assessment of the effects of the activity of the installation concerned on the environment and on human health must be an integral part of the procedures for granting or reconsidering a permit to operate such an installation under the IED.

Such a prior assessment of the effects of the installation’s activity on the environment and on human health must be considered effectively and in a timely manner by the authority responsible for granting or reconsidering that permit. This must occur before the permit is granted or reconsidered.

In its judgment, the Court also ruled that the operator of an IED installation must, throughout that installation’s period of operation, continuously assess the effects of the installation’s activities on the environment and on human health.

In the context of infringement procedure INFR(2013)21773, the Commission is currently assessing the conformity (i) of Italian legislation and (ii) of the permit granted to the Taranto steel plant via decree n. 436 of 25 July 2025 with EU legislation, namely with the IED.
